# @zakkster/lite-ohlc

Zero-allocation OHLCV candle store for live charts. A power-of-two ring of six
Float64 columns (t, o, h, l, c, v), a fused 4-lane segment tree (min low, max
high, max volume, sum volume) over the closed bars, and an O(1) live (forming)
bar kept outside the tree. It answers "what are the bounds / the decimated
buckets of this visible range" without scanning the whole history, and takes
ticks without allocating. Single-file ESM, zero runtime dependencies.

## Status: 1.0.0

## Install and import

    npm install @zakkster/lite-ohlc

    import { OhlcSeries, CANDLE_STRIDE, BOUNDS_STRIDE, BUCKET_STRIDE } from '@zakkster/lite-ohlc';

    const series = new OhlcSeries(4096, 60);      // capacity (power of two), interval
    const bar = new Float64Array(CANDLE_STRIDE);  // [t, o, h, l, c, v]
    bar.set([1000, 10, 12, 9, 11, 500]);
    series.setLiveFrom(bar);                      // forming bar, O(1) per tick
    bar.set([1060, 11, 13, 11, 12, 300]);
    series.setLiveFrom(bar);                      // later time: closes 1000, new live bar
    const bnd = new Float64Array(BOUNDS_STRIDE);
    series.boundsInto(0, series.count - 1, bnd);

## API (1.0.0)

Named exports: VERSION '1.0.0'; CANDLE_STRIDE 6; BOUNDS_STRIDE 9; BUCKET_STRIDE 7;
MIN_CAPACITY 2; MAX_CAPACITY 4194304 (2^22); MAX_BUCKETS 1048576 (2^20); class OhlcSeries.

Bars are addressed by LOGICAL index 0..count-1, 0 = oldest. A candle is always
[t, o, h, l, c, v].

new OhlcSeries(capacity, interval)
- capacity: integer power of two in [2, 4194304]. interval: finite, > 0, metadata
  only (never used to validate or align times).
- TypeError if either is not a number; RangeError if out of range.

Getters (all readonly):
- version: bumped on every successful write or clear; wraps at 2^30.
- interval, oldestTime, latestTime: doubles (cold, box once). oldestTime and
  latestTime are NaN when empty.
- capacity, count (closed + live, 0..capacity), hasLive.

Writes (all return this; hot = reads a caller-owned Float64Array, zero alloc):
- appendBarFrom(buf, off = 0): append a CLOSED bar from buf[off..off+5].
- setLiveFrom(buf, off = 0): set the LIVE bar from buf[off..off+5].
- appendBar(t, o, h, l, c, v), setLive(t, o, h, l, c, v): cold scalar wrappers, all
  six required (TypeError if any is not a number).
- clear(): O(1), forgets every bar including the live one, bumps version.

Searches (hot, binary search, O(log n); return a logical index or -1):
- lowerBoundFrom(buf, off = 0): first index with time >= buf[off].
- upperBoundFrom(buf, off = 0): LAST index with time <= buf[off].
- lowerBound(x), upperBound(x): cold scalar forms; non-number or non-finite x -> -1.
- -1 also means: series empty, or no bar qualifies. buf[off] must satisfy
  0 <= off < buf.length (RangeError otherwise).

Range queries (i0, i1 inclusive logical indices; the live bar is included):
- boundsInto(i0, i1, out, off = 0) -> n. Writes 9 doubles:
  [minLow, maxHigh, maxVol, open(i0), close(i1), sumVol, i0, i1, n].
  Returns n = i1 - i0 + 1. Invalid range (non-integer, i0 < 0, i0 > i1, i1 >= count)
  writes [NaN, NaN, NaN, NaN, NaN, 0, -1, -1, 0] and returns 0. Needs
  off + 9 <= out.length (RangeError, even for an invalid range).
- copyRangeInto(i0, i1, out, off = 0) -> n. Writes 6 doubles per bar
  [t, o, h, l, c, v], oldest first. Invalid range -> 0, nothing written. Valid
  range but off + 6 * n > out.length -> RangeError, nothing written.
- decimateInto(i0, i1, B, out, off = 0) -> buckets written. With n = i1 - i0 + 1,
  bucket k covers [i0 + ceil(k*n/B), i0 + ceil((k+1)*n/B) - 1]. Each non-empty bucket,
  ascending k, writes 7 doubles:
  [t_first, o_first, max h, min l, c_last, sum v, k].
  Empty buckets (only when n < B) write nothing, so k can skip values. Returns
  min(n, B). Invalid range -> 0, nothing written. B must be an integer in
  [1, 1048576] and off + 7 * B <= out.length, else RangeError (even for an invalid
  range). Slots past off + 7 * written are untouched.

Errors: a wrong container type (buf / out not a Float64Array) is a TypeError; a bad
offset, bad capacity or interval, invalid candle, out-of-order time or short output is a
RangeError. Every throw fires before any state write (a byte-identical no-op).
Queries with a bad VALUE (bad index range, non-finite search key) do not throw:
they return 0 or -1.

## Last-bar rule (time ordering)

Times are compared only against the NEWEST bar. Equal time replaces it; a later time
appends (closing any live bar as-is); an earlier time throws RangeError. There are
no mid-history edits and no out-of-order inserts.
- appendBarFrom, equal time: the newest bar is replaced and is CLOSED (a live bar
  becomes closed).
- setLiveFrom, equal time: the newest bar is overwritten and is LIVE (a closed
  newest bar reopens).
- Later time: any live bar is closed unchanged, the new bar is pushed; when the
  ring is full the oldest bar is evicted first.
- Empty series: any time is accepted.

## Validation rule (every write)

All six values must be finite (NaN and +-Infinity rejected), l <= o <= h,
l <= c <= h, and 0 <= v <= Number.MAX_VALUE / (4 * capacity) (the cap keeps the
volume sums finite). Failure is RangeError. A -0 is stored as +0. Time is any
finite double (no interval alignment).

## Decimation paths (settled, ROADMAP D5)

decimateInto keeps two paths: when n < B * log2(capacity) it scans linearly,
otherwise it runs one fused tree query per bucket. A given query always takes the
same path. t, o, h, l, c and k are byte-identical across the two paths. Volume
(sum v) is byte-identical for integer volumes whose sums stay below 2^53; otherwise
(fractional volumes, or integer sums at or past 2^53) the scan sums sequentially and
the tree pairwise, so the last bits can differ.

## Zero-GC and complexity

- Complexity is algorithmic, by construction (not benchmarked): setLiveFrom O(1) for
  a same-time update (a new later bar closes the previous live bar: one O(log n)
  tree walk); appendBarFrom O(log n); lowerBound / upperBound O(log n); boundsInto
  O(log n); decimateInto O(B log capacity) on the tree path, O(n + B) on the scan path;
  copyRangeInto O(n); clear O(1).
- The *From methods, the searches, boundsInto, copyRangeInto, decimateInto and the
  integer getters never allocate. Numeric return values are small integers; the writes return this.
- The scalar wrappers (appendBar, setLive, lowerBound, upperBound) box each
  fractional or large argument (up to six per appendBar / setLive call), and the
  double getters (interval, oldestTime, latestTime) box their result once per read;
  use the
  *From forms and a preallocated Float64Array in a frame loop.
- Gates (run log 2026-10-21, Node v26.8.2, macOS, load 2.3-3.0, quiet-lock):
  npm test 95/95; zerobox 10/10 (gate threshold <= 0.1 B/op); torture with 1e6
  setLiveFrom + 1e5 appendBarFrom + 1e5 boundsInto + 1e5 decimateInto -> GC major 0,
  minor 0; retention 1000 cycles -> 0 retained; a 30-run zerobox loop -> 0 fails.
  No timing or throughput figures are published.

## Gotchas

- count includes the live bar. Closed bars = count - (hasLive ? 1 : 0). count never
  exceeds capacity; a full ring evicts the oldest bar on every new later time.
- Logical indices shift when the oldest bar is evicted: an index held across a write
  may refer to a different bar. Compare `version` to detect changes.
- version wraps at 2^30; compare for equality, not ordering.
- The live bar is outside the tree and is folded into bounds / decimate in O(1); the
  tree covers closed bars only. clear() does not reset the tree (stale leaves are
  unreachable).
- A reopened bar (setLiveFrom at the same time as a closed newest bar) is simply live
  again; count is unchanged and no other bar moves; the bar takes the new values.
- Pass a Float64Array exactly: a Float32Array or plain array throws TypeError.
- interval is metadata. Nothing checks that times step by interval.

## Composability

Planned duck-typed source contract for @zakkster/lite-charts (no released lite-charts
version consumes it yet): version, interval, count, oldestTime, latestTime, lowerBound,
upperBound, boundsInto, decimateInto, copyRangeInto.

## What this is not

No viewport or pan/zoom state, no hit-testing, no object pool, no Fenwick tree or
other prefix structure, no indicators, no rendering, no resampling of ticks into
bars, no mid-history edits. Those belong to the caller or to lite-charts.
